scope: Memory gem tiers, permanent saves, loot, crafting, combat and mobile UI

rounds.finding: A raw 100 to 101 boundary would label a 0.6 percent improvement as a new upper tier.
rounds.revision: Keep old raw 0..100 unchanged. Introduce T4 120..139 and T5 160..179, with invalid gaps. Start at 280 and 340 percent skill potency.

rounds.finding: Saved pending refinement candidates were only checked for identity, permitting fabricated promotion and simultaneous affix changes.
rounds.revision: Validate one changed attribute and its acquired tier band at both save import and direct acceptance. Add corruption regression coverage while accepting old legitimate offers.

rounds.finding: Listing T1..T5 destinations without rates concealed substantial differences in upper-tier availability. A 320px English equipment button also broke inside words.
rounds.revision: Show per-attribute conditional T4/T5 rates from the same content profile as drops, explain their denominator, and stack narrow-screen actions. Verify real equip/refine/reload flows.

rounds.finding: Reducing Dream Lace cooldown increased control actions at the expense of attacks, even with AI avoiding immune targets. Paired winning AI samples increased from 15.29 to 16.38 rounds with T5.
rounds.revision: Withdraw Dream Lace cooldown reductions. Preserve cooldown 4 and sleep caps/wards. Add self ultimate charge 15 at power T4 or 30 at T5 once per actual use, regardless of success, with charge capped at 100. Re-run combat comparisons.

rounds.finding: For upper-tier rewind, furnace and sleep, every power roll inside one tier has the same capped effect. Charging dust to change only the number would not improve the stone.
rounds.revision: Disable that power-refinement action in management UI with an explanation. Keep trait refinement, lower ordinary items and legacy pending acceptance available; preserve domain-command compatibility.

limits: Tier item appearance rates are not adopted-upgrade rates or measured player time.
Fixed parties and policies do not establish optimal builds or universal monotonic win rates.
Passing tests and design review does not prove that the farming frequency is enjoyable.
